title: De novo sequencing of an unknown monoclonal antibody using BU-MS and elucidation of the neutralizing antibody-Streptolysin O complex via cross-linking and hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry
projectDescription: The identification of protective epitopes in bacterial pathogens using mass spectrometry proteomics is essential for advancing vaccine design, especially against the backdrop of increasing antibiotic resistance. Our study introduces an innovative strategy, leveraging multi-modal mass spectrometry techniques, to decode the interaction between a neutralizing monoclonal antibody (nAb) and the Streptolysin O (SLO) toxin from Streptococcus pyogenes. By integrating XL-MS, HDX-MS, and computational modeling, we successfully identified and characterized a conserved protective epitope within SLO, providing critical insights for vaccine development. Utilizing a novel nAb sequenced through de novo bottom-up shotgun MS, we explored its binding mechanism and interaction with the SLO antigen with structural proteomics such as XL-MS and HDX-MS. This study not only clarifies the conformational epitope structure but also illuminated the antibody's unique protective mechanism mode. The epitope's high conservation (near 100%) across various S. pyogenes strains underscores its potential as a universal target for vaccine strategies. Additionally, our approach overcomes traditional limitations in epitope mapping, showcasing the power of mass spectrometry in resolving challenging antibody-antigen interfaces. Our findings represent a significant leap in understanding bacterial pathogenesis and immune defense, laying the groundwork for designing next-generation vaccines. The data generated from this study can guide the development of targeted therapies and vaccines, offering new solutions to combat severe streptococcal infections.
sampleProcessingProtocol: i).Generation of Digested Peptides for De Novo Sequencing: The neutralizing antibody (nAb) was reduced with TCEP (tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine) and alkylated with IAA (Iodoacetamide). Digestion was carried out overnight at 37°C with a mix of trypsin, chymotrypsin, elastase, and pepsin, at a 1:20 w/w enzyme-to-substrate ratio. Post-digestion, peptides were purified using a C18 column, concentrated in a SpeedVac, and reconstituted in buffer A for mass spectrometry. ii).Generation of Crosslinked Peptides: nAb and SLO were mixed in a 1:1 molar ratio in 1x PBS and incubated at 37°C with agitation. Crosslinkers (DSS-H12/D12 or DSG-H6/D6) were added for a two-hour reaction, followed by quenching with ammonium bicarbonate. The mixture was then processed through standard reduction, alkylation, and a two-step digestion using lysyl endopeptidase and trypsin. iii).HDX-MS Experiment: HDX was performed on SLO in the presence and absence of nAb in PBS or HDX labeling buffer (D2O-based). Samples were incubated at various time points (0s, 60s, 1800s, and 9000s), quenched, and subjected to online pepsin digestion at 4°C. Digested samples were then processed for LC-MS analysis.
dataProcessingProtocol: i).Analysis of Peptides for De Novo Sequencing: Peptides were analyzed using a Q Exactive HF-X mass spectrometer. Data were processed with three de novo sequencing algorithms (CasaNova, SuperNova, MEM). A cumulative MS score for each peptide was calculated based on the positional evidence vector, considering fragment ion counts. ii).Search of Crosslinked Peptides Using pLink2: The LC-MS data of crosslinked peptides were analyzed using pLink2 search engine. The search parameters included applied linkers' modifications and the sequences of the heavy and light chains of nAb and SLO. The top crosslinked peptides were visualized using xiSPEC. iii).Analysis of HDX-MS Results Using HDExaminer and Deuteros: HDX-MS data were processed using HDExaminer and Deuteros 2.0. Analysis focused on comparing change of deuterium incorporation between Apo (unbound) and nAb-bound states, using observed mass differences. The results were visualized through various plots, and protected peptide residues were projected onto the 3D structure of SLO.
keywords: Host-pathogen interaction; antibody-antigen binding; mass spectrometry; structural proteomics
